
The concentration of the samples has been computed using the calibration curve in the [section above](#calibration).
The distribution of the concentration of the samples is shown below.

```{r}
cl <- unique(SumExp::col_df(measurements_se)$Class)
n_class <- length(cl)
max_nchar_chem <- max(nchar(cl))
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: !expr 'max_nchar_chem * 0.1 + 2'
#| fig-width: !expr 'n_class * 0.4 + 0.7'
#| out-width: !expr 'paste0(n_class * 4 + 7, "%")'
show_df <- SumExp::as_tibble(measurements_se)
show_df_by_chem <- split(show_df, show_df$chem_name)
for(df1 in show_df_by_chem) {
  p <- ggplot(df1) +
    geom_boxplot(aes(x = Class, y = conc, fill = Class)) +
    labs(
      title = df1$chem_name[1],
      x = labelled::get_label_attribute(df1$Class),
      y = labelled::get_label_attribute(df1$conc),
    ) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1)) +    # Vertical x-axis
    theme(legend.position = "none") +      # No legend
    scale_y_log10()
  print(p)
}
```
